Customer Engagement Dashboard Documentation

OVERVIEW
The Customer Engagement Dashboard is a comprehensive analytics tool designed to help businesses understand and improve their customer relationships. It provides insights into customer behavior, engagement levels, and actionable recommendations for business growth. KPI TILES
The dashboard features four main KPI (Key Performance Indicator) tiles:

1

TILES
The dashboard features four main KPI (Key Performance Indicator) tiles:

1 Total Customers
- Displays the complete count of customers in your database
- Helps track business growth over time
- Includes both active and inactive customers
- Updated in real-time as new customers are added

2

inactive customers
- Updated in real-time as new customers are added

2 Average Engagement Score
- Shows the mean engagement score across all customers
- Scores range from 1-10 (10 being highest engagement)
- Calculated using RFM analysis (Recency, Frequency, Monetary)
- Good benchmark: scores above 7 indicate healthy customer relationships

3

Monetary)
- Good benchmark: scores above 7 indicate healthy customer relationships

3 Average Days Since Activity
- Measures how recently customers have interacted with your business
- Lower numbers indicate more active customer base
- Helps identify if customers are becoming less engaged over time
- Benchmark: under 30 days average is excellent

4

engaged over time
- Benchmark: under 30 days average is excellent

4 Re-engagement Opportunities
- Count of customers who can potentially be won back
- Typically customers with medium-low engagement who haven't churned completely
- These represent your best ROI for marketing campaigns
- Focus area for retention strategies

ENGAGEMENT PYRAMID
The engagement pyramid is a visual representation of your customer base segmentation:

High Engagement Customers (Top of Pyramid)
- Engagement scores: 8-10
- Characteristics: Recent activity (within 30 days), frequent purchases, high transaction values
- Behavior: Respond well to marketing, likely to refer others, high lifetime value
- Strategy: Retain through VIP programs, exclusive offers, personalized service
- Typical percentage: 20-30% of customer base

Medium Engagement Customers (Middle of Pyramid)
- Engagement scores: 5-7
- Characteristics: Moderate activity (30-90 days), occasional purchases, average transaction values
- Behavior: Mixed response to marketing, potential for growth, price-sensitive
- Strategy: Targeted campaigns, product recommendations, limited-time offers
- Typical percentage: 40-50% of customer base

Low Engagement Customers (Base of Pyramid)
- Engagement scores: 1-4
- Characteristics: Inactive (90+ days), rare purchases, low transaction values
- Behavior: Poor response to marketing, at risk of churning, may have unresolved issues
- Strategy: Win-back campaigns, surveys, special discounts, direct outreach
- Typical percentage: 20-30% of customer base

CUSTOMER TABLE
The main customer table displays detailed information about each customer:

Columns Explained:
- Customer ID: Unique identifier for each customer
- Customer Name: Full name of the customer
- Engagement Score: Calculated score from 1-10 based on RFM analysis
- Engagement Level: Categorical classification (High/Medium/Low)
- Last Activity Date: Most recent interaction with your business
- Days Since Activity: Number of days since last interaction
- Total Transactions: Lifetime number of purchases
- Total Spent: Lifetime monetary value of customer
- Average Order Value: Mean transaction amount
- RFM Scores: Individual Recency, Frequency, and Monetary scores

FILTERS AND SEARCH
The dashboard includes powerful filtering capabilities:

Date Range Filter:
- Filter customers by specific time periods
- Useful for seasonal analysis
- Can show trends over different quarters or years

Engagement Level Filter:
- Quickly segment customers by High/Medium/Low engagement
- Helps focus on specific customer groups
- Essential for targeted campaign planning

Search Functionality:
- Search by customer name or ID
- Quick way to find specific customers
- Supports partial matches

Advanced Filters:
- Transaction value ranges
- Days since activity ranges
- RFM score combinations
- Custom date ranges

ENGAGEMENT SCORING METHODOLOGY
The engagement scoring system uses RFM analysis:

Recency (R) - 40% weight:
- How recently did the customer make a purchase

40% weight:
- How recently did the customer make a purchase - Score 1-5: 5 = very recent (within 7 days), 1 = very old (over 365 days)
- Recent customers are more likely to purchase again

Frequency (F) - 30% weight:
- How often does the customer make purchases. - Score 1-5: 5 = very frequent (weekly), 1 = very rare (once per year)
- Frequent customers show loyalty and engagement

Monetary (M) - 20% weight:
- How much does the customer spend

(M) - 20% weight:
- How much does the customer spend - Score 1-5: 5 = high spender (top 20%), 1 = low spender (bottom 20%)
- High-value customers contribute more to revenue

Activity Type - 10% weight:
- Quality of customer interactions
- Considers email opens, website visits, support interactions
- Meaningful engagement beyond just purchases

DASHBOARD FEATURES
Interactive Elements:
- Click on pie chart segments to filter the table
- Sort table columns by clicking headers
- Hover over charts for detailed tooltips
- Export data to CSV for further analysis

Responsive Design:
- Works on desktop, tablet, and mobile devices
- Optimized for different screen sizes
- Touch-friendly interface for mobile users

Real-time Updates:
- Data refreshes automatically
- Shows latest customer activity
- Reflects recent transactions and interactions

BUSINESS INSIGHTS
Key Metrics to Monitor:
1

BUSINESS INSIGHTS
Key Metrics to Monitor:
1 Engagement score trends over time
2. Customer distribution across engagement levels
3. Days since activity patterns

4 Re-engagement opportunity counts

Warning Signs:
- Decreasing average engagement scores
- Increasing days since activity
- Growing low engagement customer segment
- Declining high engagement customer count

Success Indicators:
- Stable or improving engagement scores
- Balanced customer distribution
- Active customer base (low days since activity)
- Growing high engagement segment

ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS
For High Engagement Customers:
- Implement loyalty programs
- Offer exclusive products or early access
- Provide premium customer service
- Ask for referrals and testimonials
- Upsell premium products or services

For Medium Engagement Customers:
- Send personalized product recommendations
- Create targeted email campaigns
- Offer limited-time promotions
- Engage through social media
- Provide educational content

For Low Engagement Customers:
- Launch win-back campaigns with special offers
- Send surveys to understand their needs
- Provide helpful resources and content
- Make direct contact via phone or email
- Offer significant discounts or incentives

CAMPAIGN STRATEGIES
Retention Campaigns:
- Focus on high engagement customers
- Emphasize value and appreciation
- Provide exclusive benefits
- Maintain regular but not overwhelming communication

Growth Campaigns:
- Target medium engagement customers
- Focus on increasing purchase frequency
- Highlight product benefits and features
- Use social proof and testimonials

Win-back Campaigns:
- Target low engagement customers
- Acknowledge their absence
- Offer compelling incentives
- Address potential issues or concerns
- Make it easy to re-engage

TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
Data Sources:
- Customer transaction database
- Website analytics
- Email marketing platforms
- Customer service interactions
- Social media engagement

Update Frequency:
- Real-time for new transactions
- Daily batch updates for calculated metrics
- Weekly updates for engagement scores
- Monthly updates for trend analysis

Performance Metrics:
- Dashboard load time: under 3 seconds
- Data refresh rate: every 5 minutes
- Export functionality: CSV, Excel formats
- Mobile responsiveness: all screen sizes

TROUBLESHOOTING
Common Issues:
- Slow loading: Check internet connection and database performance
- Missing data: Verify data source connections
- Incorrect scores: Review RFM calculation parameters
- Filter not working: Clear browser cache and refresh

Data Quality:
- Regular data validation checks
- Duplicate customer detection
- Missing data identification
- Outlier detection and handling

BEST PRACTICES
Dashboard Usage:
- Review KPIs daily
- Analyze trends weekly
- Plan campaigns monthly
- Conduct deep analysis quarterly

Data Interpretation:
- Consider seasonal factors
- Account for business changes
- Compare to industry benchmarks
- Track improvement over time

Campaign Planning:
- Segment customers appropriately
- Personalize messaging
- Test different approaches
- Measure campaign effectiveness

INTEGRATION CAPABILITIES
The dashboard can integrate with:
- CRM systems (Salesforce, HubSpot)
- Email marketing platforms (Mailchimp, Constant Contact)
- E-commerce platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce)
- Analytics tools (Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics)
- Customer service platforms (Zendesk, Freshdesk)

API ENDPOINTS
Available API endpoints for developers:
- GET /api/customers - Retrieve customer list
- GET /api/kpis - Get dashboard KPIs
- GET /api/engagement-distribution - Get engagement level distribution
- POST /api/filters - Apply custom filters
- GET /api/export - Export data in various formats

SECURITY AND PRIVACY
Data Protection:
- All customer data is encrypted
- Access controls and user permissions
- Regular security audits
- GDPR and privacy compliance
- Secure API authentication

SUPPORT AND MAINTENANCE
Regular Updates:
- Monthly feature enhancements
- Quarterly performance optimizations
- Annual major version releases
- Continuous security patches

Support Channels:
- In-app help documentation
- Email support for technical issues
- Video tutorials and training materials
- Community forums for best practices

- Create exclusive VIP experiences (early access, dedicated support). - Personalize offers based on past behavior and purchase history. - Regularly request feedback and implement changes. 4. Strengthening Medium Engagement Segment
- Run personalized recommendation campaigns

- Monitor “at-risk” customers with low scores and long inactivity. - Reach out proactively before they churn. - Offer meaningful incentives (loyalty points, free upgrades). 6

# Agent Knowledge Base (Sales and Inventory)

This file provides practical, actionable guidance the chatbot uses to answer questions when you tag @sales or @inventory. Content is embedded with tags sales_agent and inventory_agent for tag-filtered retrieval. ## Core Principles
- Be specific and actionable. Prefer steps, checklists, and measurable targets. - Use the simplest metric that answers the question; avoid jargon. - Prioritize quick wins first; then structural long-term improvements

jargon. - Prioritize quick wins first; then structural long-term improvements # Sales Strategy and Execution (@sales)

## Growth Levers
- Traffic: Increase qualified top-of-funnel (TOFU) via SEO, paid search, partner referrals. - Conversion: Reduce friction in the funnel; improve message-market fit and objection handling. - AOV/Monetization: Bundles, cross-sell, upsell, tiered pricing, add-ons. - Retention: Lifecycle messaging, reactivation campaigns, value moments

pricing, add-ons. - Retention: Lifecycle messaging, reactivation campaigns, value moments ## Funnel Optimization Checklist
1. Define a single, consistent value proposition across ads, landing pages, and sales calls. 2. Remove friction on lead capture (fewer fields, clear CTA, social proof). 3. Measure each stage: visit → lead → MQL → SQL → meeting → proposal → closed-won. 4. Identify the steepest drop-off; run 2 experiments per week there (copy, offer, CTA, proof). 5

2 experiments per week there (copy, offer, CTA, proof). 5 Standardize discovery: problem, impact, use case, timeline, decision process, budget. ## Sales Pipeline and Forecasting
- Pipeline Coverage: 3x–4x of target; segment by stage, owner, and age. - Forecast Hygiene: stage probability × deal amount; auto-flag stale deals (no activity >14 days). - Velocity: time-in-stage; auto-assign tasks to unblock (exec sponsor, trial extension, technical deep-dive)

- Cohorts: analyze retention by acquisition month and channel. - Activation Milestones: define 3 key actions within first week; trigger nudges when missed. - Churn Mitigation: outreach within 24 hours of negative usage inflection; offer success session. ## Metrics & Targets

- Add social proof above-the-fold (logos, testimonials) on top landing pages. - Add “next step” CTA on thank-you pages (book a demo, download playbook)

- Q: How to improve win rate fast. A: Standardize discovery, map 3 killer objections with talk tracks, add customer proof in proposals, and enforce a 48-hour follow-up SLA. - Q: What’s a good pipeline coverage. A: 3–4x of quarterly target; segment by stage and owner; below 2. 5x indicates risk. - Q: Best way to raise AOV

5x indicates risk. - Q: Best way to raise AOV A: Bundles, anchor pricing, add-ons at checkout; test 2 offers per week and measure attach rate. # Inventory and Operations (@inventory)

## Replenishment Fundamentals
- Reorder Point (ROP) = Avg Daily Demand × Lead Time + Safety Stock

= Avg Daily Demand × Lead Time + Safety Stock - Safety Stock approximations:
  - Normal demand: z × sqrt(lead_time_days × σ_demand^2 + demand^2 × σ_lead_time^2)
  - Simple: service_level_factor × demand_std_dev × sqrt(lead_time_days)
- Review Policies: continuous review (ROP) vs periodic review (order-up-to). ## EOQ and Ordering Costs
- EOQ = sqrt((2 × D × S) / H)
  - D: annual demand, S: order cost, H: holding cost per unit per year

S: order cost, H: holding cost per unit per year - Use EOQ for stable demand SKUs to balance ordering vs holding costs. ## ABC–XYZ Segmentation
- ABC (value): A = top ~20% revenue, B = next ~30%, C = remaining ~50%. - XYZ (predictability): X = low variability, Y = moderate, Z = high variability. - Policy Matrix:
  - AX: tight control, frequent review, low safety stock. - AZ: supplier agreements, higher safety stock, flexible lead times

- AZ: supplier agreements, higher safety stock, flexible lead times - CZ: minimize on-hand, consider make-to-order or discontinue. ## Demand Planning and S&OP
- Forecast Hierarchy: item → category → region; reconcile top-down and bottom-up. - Promotional Lifts: isolate promo impact; avoid contaminating base demand. - S&OP Cadence: monthly cycle; track forecast error (MAPE, WAPE), bias, service levels

monthly cycle; track forecast error (MAPE, WAPE), bias, service levels ## Vendor and Lead Time Management
- Lead Time Reduction: dual sourcing, pre-qualification, safety agreements. - Reliability: measure OTIF (On-Time-In-Full); penalize chronic underperformance. - MOQ vs Holding Cost: simulate cash impact; align negotiations with EOQ/ABC tiers

Holding Cost: simulate cash impact; align negotiations with EOQ/ABC tiers ## Inventory Risk and Actions
- Stockout Risk: high when variability or lead time is high; raise safety stock; coordinate with marketing to dampen demand spikes. - Dead Stock: <1 unit/week for 90 days; apply markdown ladder or bundle with high-velocity SKUs. - Excess Stock: run targeted promotions; shift inventory across locations if transfer cost < markdown loss. ## Operational Playbooks
